normal.name: Harper
normal.text: I think it's normal. Like if we can be attached to movies or books why wouldn't we also be attached video games? I think for me my nostalgia game is Super Mario Sunshine on GameCube. I just really specific memories of playing that during the summer while Wonderwall was stuck in my head for hours.

Second only to... what, Twilight Princess's 2006 launch, I assume? The funny part is this is a 28-year-old game out-selling every new release of 2026 on shelves. Physical charts are becoming a nostalgia index — the people still buying discs are the ones buying their childhood.

normal.name: Danny 🦖
normal.text: REmake set the bar so absurdly high for video game remakes everything since has been like trying to climb mt. everest. There have been many good ones, but they can't quite clear the summit. Toys for Bob came really god damn close with Reignited. Spyro was my childhood and to see it done so well 🥹

heated.name: Plot Twist Daily
heated.text: In October 1958 physicist William Higinbotham wired an oscilloscope to an analog computer for Brookhaven National Laboratory's visitors' day. People queued to play his Tennis for Two - 14 years before Atari's Pong. What did you think the first video game was? #tech #AI
heated.media: image: Timeline: Tennis for Two played at Brookhaven in October 1958; Pong released in November 1972, 14 years later.
